answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings before a deadline. GPUs may run separate chains concurrently, but cannot shortcut the dependency between squarings within any one chain; adding clones therefore demands more full sequential work rather than reducing its elapsed time. The Wesolowski proof verifies the result compactly, while willow, quartz, and walnut label no computational escape from this physical time bottleneck.
